nodes.label: Attendance calculation foundation
nodes.rationale: Approved 8 Nov 2026 with the recommended default for every open question. Phases 0 through 4 are described as shipped. Phase 5 was not started in this design. Live-database facts came from read-only counts on 8 Nov 2026.

nodes.label: Legacy attendance views
nodes.rationale: Six independent computations none of which know whether a lecture was held. attendance_summary counts weekly slots, so the percentage exceeds 100 percent after the first week, and a null division never matches. student_overall_attendance counts distinct slots that have any row, so repeated marks exceed 100 percent and a skipped student leaves the denominator. The admin defaulter export selected column names the view does not have and returned 500. Both views are dropped in 0008 because a rebuilt view would freeze one policy into SQL that every consumer shares blindly.

nodes.label: attendance_calc package
nodes.rationale: Pure Python, no Flask and no SQL, so the figures can be unit-tested with hand-calculated golden values. data_access/attendance_calc.py loads the inputs. services/attendance_calc.py is the only entry point screens, exports and notifications call. Functions are deterministic and take today from the caller. Every number a screen shows comes from StudentSummary. Percentages are Decimal, rounded once, and None when nothing is countable, never 0 and never above 100. Overall and per-component figures are pooled, not the mean of subject percentages.

nodes.label: in_roster
nodes.rationale: The one roster rule: same course and class; the slot's division when it has one, otherwise the whole class; an elective requires a chosen subject; when lab batches exist the slot's batch must be in the student's batch ids; enrolment dates bound the day. fetch_lecture_roster is its SQL twin and a test keeps the two in step.

nodes.label: Saved-mark roster evidence
nodes.rationale: A mark the teacher saved is evidence the student was in that lecture, so it counts even when the roster rule says otherwise that day. A division transfer, an enrolment date, or an elective choice recorded late never hides saved marks. Only a cancelled session ignores its marks, and cancelling a marked session is refused unless the admin clears them.

nodes.label: Excuse rule
nodes.rationale: An excuse excuses an absence, nothing else. Present or Late on an excused date still counts as attended, so a student who came in during sick leave is not penalised. The recommended store is a separate attendance_excuses table with date ranges, and an excused session leaves the denominator rather than counting as present.

nodes.label: Attendance policy defaults
nodes.rationale: Unmarked lectures are excluded from the percentage and shown as a count. Late counts as present. Excused absences leave the denominator. The threshold is an institution setting defaulting to 75. The overall figure is pooled. No data is shown as a dash, never 0. Retired slots' past sessions keep counting. A faculty absence with no approved proxy stays not_marked for a human decision rather than auto-cancelling. Enrolment for phase 1 is students.created_at and, once inactive, students.updated_at, with a proper student_enrolments table left for later so division transfers keep history.

nodes.label: lecture_sessions
nodes.rationale: One row per slot and date: held, cancelled or not_marked. There is no scheduled status, because future lectures have no row until something is known. ON DELETE RESTRICT is on purpose: a slot with sessions cannot be deleted, so the admin single-slot delete must retire it, and a session with marks cannot be deleted. attendance.timetable_id used to cascade, which erased history. session_id stays nullable in 0007 and becomes NOT NULL in 0008 after backfill. marked_by references faculty.id while timetable.faculty_id references faculty.user_id; the app keeps them equal by convention.

nodes.label: Holiday as absence of a session
nodes.rationale: A holiday is the absence of a session, so it is in no denominator. Close-day creates no row for it. A lecture marked on a holiday, a makeup class, gets a held row and counts. Dated and recurring weekday holidays are honoured through academic_rules.holidays. is_working_day is shared with the generator. institution_holidays had been used by the generator and availability rules, never by attendance.

nodes.label: Nightly close-day job
nodes.rationale: Inserts not_marked for active slots on a working day of the right weekday inside the current semester when no session row exists. It never creates held rows and never touches a row that exists. Re-running is idempotent. It writes one audit row with the counts and never prints names.

nodes.label: Substitution taught_by
nodes.rationale: taught_by is the approved proxy_log row for that slot and date, otherwise the slot faculty. Marking permission is the slot owner or taught_by for that date. Percentages do not depend on who taught. proxy_assignments has no timetable_id and is not used.

nodes.label: Historical session backfill
nodes.rationale: Backfill creates held sessions only for dates that already have marks. It never creates not_marked rows for the past, because nothing records which past lectures were held, so percentages before phase 1 use marked lectures only. Anomalies, including the 10 Feb 2026 weekday mismatch, are reported and still linked. The recommended treatment of those four live rows is to backfill them as held, because that is what was marked.

nodes.label: Device absent fill
nodes.rationale: The old mobile upload wrote a row only for a face-detected student, so everyone else was neither present nor absent. Close-day now writes Absent for roster students a device did not detect on a held mobile session, so a face-marked lecture has a full roster. Teacher-marked sessions are left alone, because a teacher's form says who it covers while a device only says who it saw. The relaxed slot resolver and non-today dates were left in place.

nodes.label: Attendance calculation phases
nodes.rationale: Each phase ships and is tested on its own so the suite stays green between phases. Phase 0 is the pure module. Phase 1 records sessions. Phase 2 moves student and defaulter screens. Phase 3 moves reports, the mobile roster and the absent fill. Phase 4 makes session_id NOT NULL and drops both views. Phase 1 as shipped left the mobile permission check unchanged; phase 3 closed it. On 9 Nov 2026 college_timetable_db was at 0007 with every mark linked, and 0008 had not been applied.

The phase 4 as-shipped note says test_migration_baseline.py named in section 4 does not exist, and names tests/unit/test_attendance_views_revision.py instead.
